author: Aleksey Razdolgin
title: Last Tuesday, Himax Technologies (NASDAQ: HIMX ) reported in
text:
Last Tuesday, Himax Technologies (NASDAQ: HIMX ) reported in-line earnings results for Q4 and the full fiscal year of 2017. Over the year, the company’s stock has been moving in both directions, as the investors saw the increased volatility in Himax’s shares due to the positive news by the end of the year that pushed the stock to its 52-week high, and due to the increased short-sell interest that created a bearish sentiment around the company, which made its shares to quickly depreciate in value in a matter of weeks. 
If you follow my profile , you know that I have been bullish on Himax since 2016. Over the last year and a half, the company has been a successful investment making more than 30% return for my portfolio. But as the time goes by, I believe that market currently offers far more attractive investments with better opportunities. 
When we look at Himax’s business, we will see that the company greatly as the company announced a number of new deals that have a potential to benefit its shareholders in the long-term. In fact, the exponential growth of its stock occurred in Autumn, which was mainly thanks to the company’s deal with Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) to supply wafer-level optics technology to the latest iPhone X. In addition, in November, the earnings report for Q3 has been released , which was well received by the investors, as it was the only quarter of the fiscal year, when the company beat its earnings per share and a revenue estimates. But besides that, there were no significant news or announcements that could have increase the value of Himax’s shares. Because of that, in early December, the advisory short-selling firm Citron made a tweet about Himax being a fraud, which served as a catalyst for a downward trend that brought the company’s stock around the 52-week low.
